newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bond yield curve steepens further.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bond yield curve steepens further.

text.p: *The Australian bond yield curve steepened again as the long end came under intense pressure following a huge sell-off in U.S. Treasuries, wiping out Wednesday's rate cut-led rally.
*November labour force report at 11.30 a.m. (0030 GMT).
The Australian bond yield curve steepened again as the long end came under intense pressure following a huge sell-off in U.S. Treasuries, wiping out Wednesday's rate cut-led rally.

The three/10-year physical bond yield spread spiked up to nearly 100 basis points after putting on some 30 basis points in the past two days as the short-end outperformed, having the protection of the cut in official interest rates to 6.0 percent.
Overseas investors were seen as heavy sellers of U.S. Treasuries, pushing the yield on the 30-year bond up to 6.63 percent, 14 basis points higher than Tuesday's New York close.

The sell-off was triggered by a Wall Street Journal article, quoting Goldman Sachs International vice chairman Robert Hormats as saying that the days of big buying by the Japanese might be coming to an end. Later in an interview with Reuters Financial Television Hormats said that recent U.S. current account numbers suggest there could be a tapering off of Japanese purchases of U.S. Treasuries, but he does not expect any major pullback.
Locally, the November labour force report is due at 11.30 a.m. (0030 GMT). Median forecasts are for a 10,000 employment rise while the unemployment rate is seen at 8.7 percent.

Local long bonds underperformed the rest of the dollar bloc, with Canada and New Zealand debt both taking their leads from the U.S. while shorts continued sharp spread narrowing following Wednesday's surprise rate cut by the RBA.
